description.value: The study examined whether imagery-focused emotion regulation during conditioned reward cues influences decision-making under risk and associated BOLD responses in reward-related neural circuitry.

spans.text: To investigate this question, we asked participants to engage in imagery-focused regulation strategies during the presentation of a cue that preceded a financial decision-making phase.

description.value: An fMRI experimental paradigm included cue and decision phases. Thirty-five right-handed volunteers participated; five datasets were excluded, leaving 30 participants for final analysis.

spans.text: We investigated the effect of cognitive regulation on risk-taking and its neural correlates using a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) experimental paradigm that included both a cue and a decision phase.

decision-making under risk

description.value: Participants viewed a conditioned stimulus and one of three cognitive instructions, then chose between risky and safe monetary lotteries for CS+ trials or between stamps for CS− trials.

spans.text: The decision phase followed the cue presentation and comprised either a selection between risky and safe monetary lotteries (CS+ trials) or a non-monetary control decision between two different stamps (CS− trials; Fig. 1 ).
CS+
The conditioned stimulus indicated if the trial presented an opportunity to earn money (CS+) or not (CS−).

description.value: Participants viewed a slot-machine conditioned stimulus paired with the instruction Look, Relax, or Excite, then chose between a risky monetary lottery and a guaranteed safe monetary amount with equivalent expected value.

spans.text: For CS+ trials, participants chose between two monetary options: a gamble (risky option) and a guaranteed amount (safe option) that varied with respect to probability and amount.
CS−
The conditioned stimulus indicated if the trial presented an opportunity to earn money (CS+) or not (CS−).

description.value: Participants viewed a stamp-machine conditioned stimulus paired with the instruction Look, Relax, or Excite, then chose between two postage stamps with different patterns and no monetary value.

spans.text: For CS− trials, the decision carried no affective significance, as participants chose between two different representations of postage stamps with no monetary value.
There were three such instructions: “Look”, “Relax” and “Excite”.
